heat.title: Heat map and Heat Score
heat.body: Each hexagon (about 135 m across) gets a Heat Score from 0 to 100, compared with its own area. Daytime surface heat comes from Landsat 8/9 and HLS at 30 m, night heat from MODIS, sharpened with ECOSTRESS when a pass is available. Sealed ground, green cover and water come from ESA WorldCover. A hexagon without data is shown as “no data”, never guessed.

zones.title: Hot zones and their causes
zones.body: The hottest quarter of hexagons are grouped into connected zones and ranked; zones within 3 points are shown as near-ties. Each zone's causes come from a model fitted on the city's own hexagons, and the explanation is written from those numbers.

air.title: Temperature and forecast
air.body: Current readings come from the Open-Meteo model, cross-checked with NASA GEOS-FP. Normals and recent observed weather come from NASA POWER, and future warming in projections from NASA NEX-GDDP-CMIP6. “Feels like” uses the NOAA heat index. In Bangladesh, heat levels follow BMD thresholds; they are not official warnings.

aq.title: Air quality
aq.body: Measured PM2.5 comes from OpenAQ stations. Forecasts come from NASA GEOS-CF and Open-Meteo and are labelled as models. The AQI uses the US EPA 2024 PM2.5 breakpoints. A sensor you add sends its own real readings; nothing is simulated.

cooling.title: Cooling estimates
cooling.body: Each +1 % of tree canopy in a km² lowers daytime surface temperature by roughly 0.1–0.2 °C; cool roofs about 0.04 °C per 1 % of a km². Tree cooling ramps up as trees grow. Projections are ranges and estimates, never promises; tree CO₂ is an estimate, not an offset.

farm.title: Farmer alerts
farm.body: Ten fixed rules run on the forecast, NASA POWER rainfall, NASA SMAP soil wetness, NASA IMERG rain from the last 72 hours and the NASA LIS/OTD lightning climatology, following BMD, BRRI and DAE guidance. Atmos X never gives pesticide doses.

community.title: Your account and privacy
community.body: Your account, actions, trees and teams are kept on Atmos X servers so they work on any device. Public places are rounded to about 100 m, and your photos stay private unless you post them. The demo community uses invented people and teams and never mixes with real leaderboards.

nurseries.title: Nurseries and the store
nurseries.body: Nursery locations come from OpenStreetMap plus a curated Dhaka list. Partner nurseries can sell saplings and planting kits through the app, paid in taka through SSLCommerz; Atmos X keeps a small commission. Points from verified trees buy products that partner companies give; points have no cash value.

checks.title: How actions are checked
checks.body: Every photo goes through fixed checks: GPS present and near the place, a plausible location, taken recently, taken in the app, not a duplicate, and content that fits the action. Anything flagged goes to a teammate or a moderator. No language model is involved.

ask.title: Ask Atmos
ask.body: Ask Atmos answers from the app's own data with fixed rules: it recognises the question, reads the same numbers you see on screen and shows its sources. It does not use a language model, so it never makes facts up.
